comparison: Perfect agreement on yeast mutation clustering data (C5, C22-C34, C72). Both evaluations find the experimental design, quantitative metrics, and statistical analysis well-supported. Reviewers explicitly praise the yeast system and whole-genome sequencing approach.

Disagreement on mutational spectrum and REV1 mechanism (C35-C41, C87, C89-C90). OpenEval accepts the mechanistic interpretation of REV1's deoxycytidyl transferase activity, while peer reviewers raise concerns about pleiotropic effects of REV1 deficiency, suggesting the mechanistic interpretation may be incomplete.

Strong agreement on UNG deletion experiments (C6, C41-C53, C78-C79). Both evaluations recognize this as a major strength providing key mechanistic insight into kataegis. Reviewers explicitly highlight the fundamental role of base excision demonstrated by these experiments.

Disagreement on I-SceI break experiments (C7, C54-C55, C73, C81, C84, C108-C109). OpenEval finds the data sufficient, but peer reviewers request additional control data (I-SceI without APOBEC3G) to fully support conclusions about mutation localization.

Disagreement on resection mechanism (C74-C77 overlap). OpenEval accepts the inference about long-zone end resection from cluster lengths, while peer reviewers challenge this interpretation, suggesting alternative explanations like increased DNA breathing in opened chromatin rather than direct resection.

Agreement on mutational signature analysis (C57-C65, C96-C97). Both evaluations accept the matching between yeast APOBEC3A/B patterns and breast cancer signatures. No concerns raised about the quantitative sequence context analysis or statistical comparisons.

Agreement on APOBEC3B/A involvement in breast cancer (C68-C71, C101, C9). Both evaluations accept the main conclusion about APOBEC3A/B role in kataegis. Reviewers find the manuscript timely and acknowledge the mechanistic insights despite overlap with concurrent work.

Partial overlap on abstract claims (C3-C4). OpenEval finds these summary claims well-supported by detailed results, while peer reviewers question the underlying mechanistic interpretation about resection, suggesting the evidence is indirect.

Agreement on APOBEC3B/A identification (C8). Both evaluations support this conclusion, with OpenEval noting convergence of multiple lines of evidence and peer reviewers accepting the signature matching as central to main conclusions.

Agreement on APOBEC3B/A as source of kataegis (C9). Both evaluations support this main conclusion, with peer reviewers describing the manuscript as presenting a concise and timely description of this role.

Agreement on strand coordination data (C34). Peer reviewers request clarification about terminology but do not question the underlying observation. Both accept the data showing clustered mutations on same strand.

Agreement on uncertainty of mechanistic speculation (C89-C90). OpenEval marks these as speculative hypotheses not directly demonstrated, while peer reviewers question the mechanistic interpretation of REV1 effects, both recognizing limitations in mechanistic conclusions.
